summary: Yes, the model is well-calibrated. The primary model (HistGradientBoostingClassifier) has Expected Calibration Error (ECE) = 0.0046 and max per-bin gap (MCE) = 0.0223 across 10 probability bins on held-out test data, with predicted probabilities tracking observed outcome frequencies closely in every bin (largest gap only ~2.2 percentage points, in a sparsely-populated bin). Applying isotonic recalibration to the GBM does not meaningfully change this (ECE = 0.0049, essentially unchanged / within noise), confirming the model's raw probabilities were already well-calibrated rather than systematically over- or under-confident; a plain Logistic Regression reference model shows a similarly small ECE (0.0083).
primary_metric_name: Expected Calibration Error (ECE, 10 equal-width bins, GBM)
direction: model is well-calibrated (ECE ~0.005, near-identity reliability curve, isotonic recalibration gives no improvement)
methodological_choices: Model: HistGradientBoostingClassifier (max_iter=300, default depth/leaf settings) chosen as 'the model' since gradient-boosted trees are a common strong tabular baseline and are known to be less inherently calibrated than linear models; Logistic Regression fit as a calibration reference point, and an isotonic-calibrated GBM (via 5-fold CalibratedClassifierCV) fit to quantify how much room for improvement exists. Preprocessing: missing categoricals imputed as 'Unknown' category, one-hot encoding for 8 categorical features, standard-scaling for 6 numeric features (fit on train only). Split: single stratified 75/25 train/test split, random_state=42 (no k-fold CV for the primary calibration read, though isotonic calibration internally uses 5-fold CV on the training set only). Calibration metric: ECE and MCE computed with 10 equal-width bins over [0,1] on the test set (a common but not unique choice; equal-frequency binning or fewer/more bins would give somewhat different numeric ECE values, though similar qualitative conclusions). No class-imbalance correction (~24% positive class) was applied since calibration, not classification threshold, is the target of the question. Brier score reported as a secondary proper-scoring-rule check consistent with the ECE finding.
